# 02.1_Secondary_plant-read_filtering_with_DIAMOND
# This step uses the paired unmapped FASTQ files generated by the STAR host-read-removal step:
# /path/to/STAR_output/sample_Unmapped.out.mate1
# /path/to/STAR_output/sample_Unmapped.out.mate2

# Residual plant-derived reads are identified by translated alignment against reviewed Viridiplantae proteins from UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot before downstream microbial classification.

# DIAMOND blastx translates nucleotide reads and aligns them against a protein reference database.




## Download and extract DIAMOND
# DIAMOND v2.0.15 was used in this workflow.
# The following commands download and extract the precompiled Linux binary.
mkdir -p "/path/to/software/diamond-v2.0.15"
cd "/path/to/software/diamond-v2.0.15"
wget "https://github.com/bbuchfink/diamond/releases/download/v2.0.15/diamond-linux64.tar.gz"
tar -xzf "diamond-linux64.tar.gz"
# Check the installed version
./diamond version


## Download the reviewed Viridiplantae protein reference
# taxonomy_id:33090 selects Viridiplantae proteins.
# reviewed:true restricts the query to reviewed UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot entries.
# The database download date should be recorded because UniProtKB is updated over time.
mkdir -p "/path/to/diamond_database"
wget \
  -O "/path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae.fasta" \
  "https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/stream?compressed=false&format=fasta&query=(taxonomy_id:33090)%20AND%20(reviewed:true)"


## Build the DIAMOND-formatted protein database
# The --db option specifies the output database path and filename prefix.
# DIAMOND adds the .dmnd extension to the resulting database.
"/path/to/software/diamond-v2.0.15/diamond" makedb \
  --in "/path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae.fasta" \
  --db "/path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae"
# Output database:
# /path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae.dmnd


## Identify Viridiplantae-hit reads using DIAMOND blastx
### create the directory for DIAMOND blastx hits
cd "/path/to/STAR_output"
mkdir -p ""02.1_secondary_mapping""

### Run DIAMOND blastx hits
# DIAMOND blastx is run separately on mate1 and mate2.
# The code block below forms one complete Bash loop.
# Copy the entire block, from "for" to "done", and run it in a terminal from the directory containing the STAR-unmapped read files.

# An e-value threshold of 1e-5 was used in this workflow.
# The thread setting may be adjusted according to the available computing resources.
for mate1 in *mate1*; do
    mate2="${mate1/mate1/mate2}"

  if [[ ! -f "$mate2" ]]; then
    echo "Paired mate2 file was not found for: $mate1" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  echo "Processing: $mate1 and $mate2"

  "/path/to/software/diamond-v2.0.15/diamond" blastx \
    --db "/path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae" \
    --query "$mate1" \
    --out ""02.1_secondary_mapping"/${mate1}.viridiplantae.blastx" \
    --evalue 1e-5 \
    --threads 8 \
    --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident evalue bitscore

  "/path/to/software/diamond-v2.0.15/diamond" blastx \
    --db "/path/to/diamond_database/swissprot_viridiplantae" \
    --query "$mate2" \
    --out ""02.1_secondary_mapping"/${mate2}.viridiplantae.blastx" \
    --evalue 1e-5 \
    --threads 8 \
    --outfmt 6 qseqid sseqid pident evalue bitscore
done
# A query read may have more than one reported alignment.
# Unique qseqid values are extracted later by the read-filtering script.


## Remove Viridiplantae-hit reads from STAR-unmapped reads and retain complete non-plant read pairs
### Install SeqKit using Conda
# SeqKit v2.10.0 was used in this workflow.
conda install -c bioconda seqkit=2.10.0
# Check the installed version
seqkit version

### Run the script for filtering Viridiplantae-hit reads
# The secondary_plant_read_filtering.sh helper script is provided in the scripts directory of this repository.
# The script extracts unique Viridiplantae-hit read IDs from the DIAMOND output, removes the corresponding reads from mate1 and mate2, and retains synchronized non-plant read pairs for downstream analyses.
# Copy the complete script to the directory containing the STAR-unmapped read files and run it in a terminal.
